s1.syndrome_frame: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes
salient_findings: Left bundle-branch block (LBBB) during stress test
key_facts: Patient in early 60s
2-week history of chest pain during exertion
Chest pain consistently presented during physical activity
Patient is a nonsmoker
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
Baseline 12-lead ECG showed no substantial abnormalities
Stress ECG developed LBBB in stage 2 at heart rate of 107 beats per minute
LBBB resolved following exercise cessation with immediate angina relief
No ischemic or memory T waves in pre- and post-exercise ECGs
Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Coronary artery spasm
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes and no coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Cardiac syndrome X
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion with normal coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Microvascular coronary disease
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain with no obstructive coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain and transient left bundle-branch block

shortlist.label: Myocardial bridging
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion with no significant coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of chest pain during exertion, absence of substantial abnormalities on baseline ECG, and normal coronary computed tomography angiography findings are consistent with Cardiac syndrome X, which is characterized by chest pain with evidence of myocardial ischemia but normal coronary arteries.

rejected.label: Coronary artery spasm
rejected.why: While coronary artery spasm could cause chest pain during exertion, the lack of ischemic or memory T waves in pre- and post-exercise ECGs makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Microvascular coronary disease
rejected.why: This condition could also cause chest pain, but the normal coronary computed tomography angiography and lack of specific evidence for microvascular disease make it less likely than Cardiac syndrome X.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of left ventricular hypertrophy or other characteristic features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the provided information.

rejected.label: Myocardial bridging
rejected.why: Myocardial bridging is a possible cause of chest pain, but the provided information does not specifically suggest this condition, and Cardiac syndrome X better explains the combination of symptoms and test results.
